enonce.question: Identify the tense in this sentence: 'They were playing football when the storm began.' Name the two tenses used.
Choose the correct tense. Every Sunday, my grandmother ____ (bake) fresh bread for the whole family.
Fill in with 'for' or 'since': We have known each other ____ 2018.
Which conditional type is this sentence? 'If you mix blue and yellow, you get green.'

Complete the sentences with the correct form of the verbs in brackets using the simple present or present continuous tense.
1. Every morning, Sarah (go) to school by bus.
2. Look! The children (play) football in the garden now.
3. My father usually (watch) the news at 8 PM.
4. Listen! Someone (knock) at the door.
5. We (not / like) spicy food.

Put the verbs in brackets into the correct tense: simple past or past continuous.
1. While I (walk) home, I (see) an old friend.
2. They (play) video games when their mother (arrive).
3. She (read) a book when the phone (ring).
4. We (wait) for the bus when it (start) to rain.
5. He (drive) to work when he (realize) he forgot his wallet.
Complete the first conditional: If the weather ____ (be) fine tomorrow, we ____ (go) to the beach.
Rewrite using the second conditional: 'I do not have a car, so I cannot drive you home.'
Correct the mistake: 'She have already visited London twice.'
Choose the correct option: 'Water ____ at one hundred degrees Celsius.' (boils / is boiling / boiled)
Rewrite with 'unless': 'If you do not water the plant, it will die.'
Put the verb in the correct tense: By the time the guests arrived, my mother ____ (finish) preparing dinner.
Give advice for each situation using a conditional. 1) Your friend is always tired in class. 2) A classmate wants to improve his English.
Complete the third conditional and explain the meaning: 'If I ____ (know) about the meeting, I ____ (attend) it.'

Complete the sentences with the correct form of the verbs in brackets using the first conditional (if + present simple, will + base verb).
1. If it (rain) tomorrow, we (stay) at home.
2. She (pass) her exam if she (study) hard.
3. They (not / go) to the party if they (not / finish) their homework.
4. If you (not / hurry), you (miss) the train.
5. We (visit) the museum if we (have) time.
Write a short paragraph of four to five sentences about your last school trip, using at least the past simple, the past continuous and the present perfect.
Write five descriptive sentences about your school. Use at least four different adjectives and appeal to at least two senses.

Read the short text and say which sentences are DESCRIPTIVE and which are NARRATIVE: (1) The lake was calm and silver under the moon. (2) Suddenly, a boy jumped into the water. (3) The trees around it were tall and dark. (4) He swam quickly to the other side.
Write a short descriptive paragraph (5-6 sentences) about your favorite room in your house. Use at least 3 adjectives to describe it.
Rewrite these weak sentences to make them more descriptive: (a) The dog was big. (b) The food was good. (c) The weather was bad.
Write a descriptive paragraph (6-8 sentences) about a member of your family. Use adjectives, the senses, and at least one simile.
Write a narrative paragraph (8-10 sentences) about a school trip. Use the past simple, at least one past continuous, and four time connectors.
Join each pair of sentences using the past continuous or the past perfect: (a) I was doing my homework. The lights went off. (b) The film started. We arrived at the cinema.
Write a narrative paragraph (8-10 sentences) about a memorable day you had with your family. Use past simple verbs and time expressions like 'last weekend', 'yesterday', 'in the morning'.
Write a short story (10-12 sentences) that teaches a lesson (a moral). Combine description and narration, and end with the moral in one sentence.
Continue this story in 8-10 sentences, keeping the past tense and adding description and time connectors: 'When I opened the old wooden box in the attic, I could not believe my eyes...'

Write a descriptive and narrative paragraph (10-12 sentences) combining description and narration. Describe your best friend and narrate a time when you helped each other. Use adjectives, past simple verbs, and time expressions.
Write a descriptive-narrative paragraph (10-12 sentences) about a stormy night you remember. Describe the setting, then narrate what happened. Keep your tenses consistent.
What kind of question is this: 'Find a word in the text that means the opposite of expensive'?
Read: 'Amir loves the sea. He goes swimming every weekend.' What does the word 'He' refer to?
Match the strategy to its purpose. A) Skimming  B) Scanning. 1) finding a specific date quickly  2) getting the general idea of a text.

Read the following short text and answer the question:

"My name is Ahmed. I am 14 years old. I live in Tunis with my family. I love playing football after school. My favorite team is Espérance de Tunis."

What is Ahmed's favorite sport?
Where in a paragraph do you most often find the main idea?

Read the short text and identify the main idea: 'Reading every day improves your vocabulary. It also strengthens your memory and helps you write better. Above all, it opens your mind to new ideas.' What is the text mainly about?
Read: 'The city council banned cars from the old centre. Since then, the air has become cleaner and the streets safer for children.' True or false, and justify: 'The ban had positive effects.'
Guess the meaning of the underlined word from context: 'The road was so narrow that only one car could pass at a time.' What does 'narrow' mean?
Read: 'Turn off the tap while brushing your teeth. Fix leaks quickly. Collect rainwater for your plants.' What is the writer's main purpose?
Read: 'Leila checked her bag three times before leaving and kept looking at the clock.' What can you infer about how Leila felt? Explain.

Read the text below and answer the questions:

"Sara is a student in a secondary school in Sfax. She gets up at 6:30 AM every day. After breakfast, she goes to school by bus. Classes start at 8:00 AM and finish at 2:00 PM. She has lunch at home and then does her homework. In the evening, she watches TV or reads a book."

a) What time does Sara wake up?

b) How does Sara go to school?

c) What does Sara do after lunch?

Read the following passage and answer the questions:

"Last weekend, I visited my grandparents in a small village near Kairouan. The weather was sunny and warm. We had a big lunch with couscous and fresh vegetables. In the afternoon, I helped my grandfather in the garden. We planted some tomatoes and watered the plants. My grandmother told me stories about the old days. It was a wonderful day."

a) Where did the person spend the weekend?

b) What was the weather like?

c) What did the person do in the garden?

d) What did the grandmother do?

Read the passage and answer the three questions. Passage: 'When Karim was ten, his family moved from a small mountain village to the busy capital. At first, the noise and the crowds frightened him, and he missed the quiet fields where he used to play. Little by little, however, he made new friends at school and discovered a large public library. Books became his refuge, and within two years he no longer wished to return to the village.' Q1: Why was Karim frightened at first? Q2: What helped him settle in? Q3: Find a word that means a safe, comforting place.

Read the passage and answer. Passage: 'Every summer, thousands of volunteers clean the beaches along the Tunisian coast. They collect plastic bottles, bags and cans that harm sea life. Local associations organise the events, while schools encourage students to take part. Although the task is tiring, the volunteers feel proud when they see the clean sand at the end of the day.' Q1: Who organises the clean-up events? Q2: Why do the volunteers feel proud? Q3: In your own words, explain the main message of the text (one sentence).

Read: 'Although the new smartphone was expensive, Nour saved for months to buy it. Yet a week later she admitted that her old phone had worked almost as well.' What is the writer suggesting about Nour's decision? Support your answer.
Is the relative clause defining or non-defining? 'My uncle, who lives in Nabeul, grows oranges.'
Choose the correct relative pronoun: 'This is the museum ____ we saw the ancient mosaics.' (which / where / who)
Choose the correct relative pronoun: 'The woman ____ teaches us history is from Bizerte.' (who / which / where)
Choose the correct relative pronoun: 'I have a friend ____ brother plays for the national team.' (who / whose / which)

Combine the two sentences using a relative clause with 'who' or 'which'.
1. The teacher is very kind. She teaches us English.
2. I bought a book. The book is about history.
Add commas if the clause is non-defining, or leave it as it is if defining: 'The novel which won the prize is now a film.' / 'Tunis which is the capital lies on the coast.'
Combine into one sentence with a relative clause: 'I bought a jacket. The jacket is made of wool.'
Correct the mistake: 'The man who he sells newspapers is very kind.'

Complete the sentences with the correct relative pronoun (who, which, that, or whose).
1. The boy ______ father is a doctor is my best friend.
2. The car ______ I bought last week is very fast.
3. The woman ______ works in the library is very helpful.
Decide whether the relative pronoun can be omitted: 'The film that we watched last night was boring.'
Combine into one sentence: 'The students passed the exam. They had worked hard.'
Complete with 'when' or 'why': 'I still remember the day ____ we won the tournament.'
Rewrite the passage to remove the repetition, using relative clauses: 'Sfax is a large city. Sfax is famous for its old medina. The medina attracts tourists. The tourists come from many countries.'

Rewrite the following sentences using non-defining relative clauses (add commas where necessary).
1. My sister who lives in Paris is a doctor.
2. The Eiffel Tower which is in Paris is very famous.
3. The students who study hard usually succeed.
Write a short paragraph of five sentences describing a person you admire, using at least three different relative pronouns (for example who, whose, that).
Join the three ideas into one clear sentence using relative clauses: 'I recommend a restaurant. It is near the harbour. Its owner cooks fresh fish.'
Is this sentence active or passive? 'The homework is corrected by the teacher.'
Which verb cannot be made passive: 'write', 'arrive', 'clean'? Explain briefly.
Identify the past participle you would need to make 'They build houses' passive.
Complete with the correct form of 'be' (present simple): The offices ____ cleaned every evening.

Rewrite the following sentences in the passive voice. Do not change the tense.
1. Someone cleans the classroom every day.
2. They built this bridge in 1990.
3. The teacher will explain the lesson tomorrow.
Change into the passive: 'The gardener waters the flowers every day.'
Change into the passive: 'A local artist painted this mural last year.'
Change into the passive (future): 'The committee will announce the results tomorrow.'
Change into the passive with a modal: 'You must submit the application before Friday.'
Correct the mistake: 'The letter was write by my father.'
Change into the passive (present perfect): 'The workers have repaired the road.'

Complete the sentences with the correct passive form of the verbs in brackets. Use the present simple or past simple tense.
1. Rice ______ (grow) in many Asian countries.
2. The Mona Lisa ______ (paint) by Leonardo da Vinci.
3. These books ______ (write) by a famous author in 2010.
Change the active sentence into the passive and explain why the passive is suitable here: 'Someone stole my wallet on the bus.'
Rewrite this news item so that the receiver of each action is the focus: 'The government has opened a new library. Workers built it in eight months. Volunteers will run reading clubs there.'
Write a short paragraph of five sentences describing how olive oil is produced in Tunisia, using at least four passive verbs.

Change the following active sentences into passive voice. Keep the same meaning and tense. Some sentences may require the use of 'by' to specify the doer.
1. People speak French in Algeria.
2. The chef is preparing a special dish for the guests.
3. The government will announce the new law soon.
Put the words in order to make a question: (you / have / ever / been / to Italy)?
Complete with 'have' or 'has': My cousins ____ already left, but their sister ____ not arrived yet.
Give the past participle of these verbs: go, write, see, eat.
Choose 'for' or 'since': He has taught mathematics ____ five years.

Complete the sentences with the present perfect form of the verbs in brackets.
1. She ______ (visit) her grandmother twice this month.
2. We ______ (not finish) our homework yet.
3. They ______ (already see) that movie.
4. He ______ (never travel) abroad.
5. I ______ (just meet) my new teacher.
Choose the correct tense: 'We ____ a wonderful film last night.' (have watched / watched)
Correct the mistake: 'She has wrote three letters this morning.'
Use the present perfect continuous: 'They ____ (wait) for the bus for twenty minutes.'
Choose the correct tense: 'I ____ my keys, so I cannot open the door.' (lost / have lost)

Put the words in the correct order to make sentences in the present perfect.
1. ever / you / seen / a lion / have ?
2. they / not / the lesson / understood / have.
3. she / her keys / lost / has.
4. we / this year / three tests / taken / have.
5. he / never / played / football / has.
Complete with the present perfect: The students ____ (not finish) their project yet.
Insert 'already', 'yet' or 'just' in the correct place: 'The train has ____ left; we missed it by seconds.'

Read this note and answer: 'Nadia moved to Sousse in 2015 and still lives there. She started her current job in 2020.' Write two sentences, one with 'for' and one with 'since', about how long she has lived in Sousse and had her job.

Read the following dialogue and fill in the blanks with the correct present perfect form of the verbs given.
A: Hi, Sam! Where have you been? I ______ (not see) you for ages!
B: Oh, I’ve been busy. I ______ (start) a new hobby.
A: Really? What is it?
B: I ______ (learn) to play the guitar. It’s great!
A: Wow! How long ______ you ______ (practice) it?
B: I ______ (practice) for two weeks now.
A: That’s impressive! Have you played for anyone yet?
B: Yes, I ______ (play) for my family twice.
Transform the sentence, keeping the same meaning: 'This is my first visit to Carthage.' Begin with 'I have never ...'.
Write a short paragraph of five sentences about the changes in your town over the last few years, using the present perfect (for example: new buildings, roads, shops).
